title: CLI entry point does not exist: mdoutline.py has no main/argparse; every spec CLI claim is untestable

title: make install / pip install -e . fails: invalid build backend 'setuptools.backends._legacy:_Backend'
description:
QA re-test t_64d567c7 @ 227c19c (Python 3.14.6, Linux).

CLAIM: Makefile target 'install: pip install -e ".[dev]"' (the documented dev bootstrap) and ADR-001 packaging posture.

ACTUAL: pyproject.toml [build-system] build-backend = 'setuptools.backends._legacy:_Backend' — module does not exist.

EVIDENCE:
  source .venv/bin/activate && make install
  -> pip._vendor.pyproject_hooks._impl.BackendUnavailable: Cannot import 'setuptools.backends._legacy'
  -> make: *** [Makefile:4: install] Error 2

Workaround used by QA: pip install pytest ruff directly (works; make check then green).

FIX: build-backend = 'setuptools.build_meta' (or 'setuptools.build_meta:__legacy__' — the real legacy path; the declared name garbles both).

SEVERITY: Important/P2 — breaks the standard install path for every fresh clone. Route: debugger.

title: make install fails: pyproject build-backend 'setuptools.backends._legacy:_Backend' does not exist
description:
QA re-test t_6b5e5c59 @ bfaf57e (Python 3.14.5, Linux, pip 26.1.2).

CLAIM TESTED: scaffold ticket T1 (566d0c1) ships a working dev install path (Makefile: 'install: pip install -e ".[dev]"').

ACTUAL: 'pip install -e ".[dev]"' aborts with BackendUnavailable: Cannot import 'setuptools.backends._legacy'. pyproject.toml:3 declares build-backend = 'setuptools.backends._legacy:_Backend' — no such module exists in setuptools. The correct legacy backend is 'setuptools.build_meta:__legacy__'.

REPRO: cd /home/lpaydat/workspace/mdoutline && make install
-> BackendUnavailable: Cannot import 'setuptools.backends._legacy'

ROOT-CAUSE PROOF: copied repo to a scratch dir, changed only the backend string to 'setuptools.build_meta:__legacy__', reran 'python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e ".[dev]"' -> success (exit 0, import mdoutline OK).

IMPACT: documented build path dead for any fresh contributor; ticket 3 (CLI entry point / packaging) will hit this immediately. Workaround exists (run pytest directly; conftest.py puts repo root on sys.path — 33 tests pass without install). Severity Important/P2, not Critical: core library functionality unaffected.

FIX: pyproject.toml:3 -> build-backend = 'setuptools.build_meta:__legacy__' (or plain 'setuptools.build_meta'). Note: conftest.py + spec say 'no packaging beyond what pytest needs', so dropping the build-backend entirely is also viable — dev decision.

title: qa: silent fallback masks operator intent - malformed MDOUTLINE_BIN now degrades to python -m mdoutline without warning (T7 regression in test-infra observability)
description:
QA re-test t_493d37a2 @ 6d78268 (Python 3.14.5, Linux, CachyOS).

CONTEXT: T7 (6d78268) changed _require_cmd_and_env (tests/conftest.py:71-84): when the strict resolver returns None, the runner now falls back to [sys.executable, '-m', 'mdoutline'] instead of raising RuntimeError. This is the designed foreign-interpreter portability behavior and the suite is green in all 3 environments (venv normal: 290 passed; venv off-PATH: 290 passed; foreign interpreter /usr/bin/python3.14: 279 passed + 11 designed script-deployment skips).

FINDING (test-infra observability, not product): the fallback is silent. Pre-T7, a malformed MDOUTLINE_BIN (e.g. '"unclosed-quote') caused a loud RuntimeError('mdoutline command not found - set MDOUTLINE_BIN or install the package') that failed the suite immediately. Post-T7, the same malformed override silently falls back to python -m mdoutline, which (because PYTHONPATH=REPO_ROOT is prepended in the runner env) tests the REPO SOURCE, not the binary the operator pointed at. An operator testing a deployed wheel with a typo'd override now gets green tests that never executed their intended target.

EVIDENCE (executed at 6d78268):
1. env MDOUTLINE_BIN='"unclosed-quote' pytest tests/test_cli.py -> 21 passed, 1 skipped, RC=0 (no warning anywhere in output).
2. env MDOUTLINE_BIN='   ' pytest tests/test_cli.py -> 22 passed, RC=0.
3. Direct probe of conftest._require_cmd_and_env with resolver forced to None: returns [sys.executable, '-m', 'mdoutline'] and executes a real outline correctly (RC=0, '- A / - B' output).

REPRO: env MDOUTLINE_BIN='"unclosed-quote' python -m pytest tests/test_cli.py -q  # passes silently, never warns

SUGGESTED FIX: emit a one-line warning to stderr (pytest terminal summary or warnings summary) when the strict resolver returns None and MDOUTLINE_BIN is set-but-unusable, distinguishing 'override set but malformed' from 'not installed'. Severity Minor/P3 (test-infra observability). Route: debugger.

title: make check / ruff check . sweeps untracked agent scratch dirs: concurrent-session .py files cause spurious test_r5 failure
description:
Context: QA re-test t_96b0cafd @ e429f4d (2026-08-17). During live testing, make check initially passed, then pytest tests/test_behavior_ruff_deadness.py::test_r5_repo_lint_and_format_green began failing with E741 in .traces/t_2a11943f/dump_bash_results.py — a scratch file written mid-session by a DIFFERENT concurrent agent task (not project code). ruff check . (and the test_r5 wrapper) lint every *.py under the repo including untracked dirs (.traces/, .driver/, .pi/), so any scratch Python file dropped by a concurrent session breaks the canonical gate.

Reproduction: touch a file with a lint error in an untracked dir, e.g. printf 'l = [l for l in range(3)]\n' > .traces/probe.py && make check  → ruff check . fails (E741), pytest suite fails test_r5_repo_lint_and_format_green.

Impact: false gate failures in shared/multi-agent workspaces; gate result depends on transient untracked files, not committed state. Committed tree verified pristine in isolated worktree: 288/288 passed, ruff clean (make check green at e429f4d).

Suggested fix (tech-lead): add .traces/.driver/.pi/.beads to ruff exclude list in pyproject.toml, or have test_r5 lint only git-tracked files (git ls-files '*.py').

Environment: Linux 6.x, Python 3.14.5, ruff from .venv, pytest 9.x, HEAD e429f4d4cb09.

title: CLI --max-depth help documents 1-6 but range is not enforced (0=empty, >6=all, RC=0)
description: QA re-test of e6f39af (t_33484ef7). Claim tested: --max-depth N documented as 'maximum heading depth to include (1-6, default: all depths)'. Actual: argparse only enforces >= 0. Evidence on fresh pip install of e6f39af: '--max-depth 0 FILE' prints nothing, RC=0 (silent empty output — likely a typo surprise); '--max-depth 7' and '--max-depth 999' print the full unfiltered outline, RC=0 (indistinguishable from no-limit default). Negative/non-int values correctly rejected with argparse error RC=2. Repro: mdoutline --max-depth 0 anyfile.md; echo $? => 0, no output. Suggested fix: argparse type validator clamping/rejecting N<1 or N>6, or correct the help text. Severity Minor: all documented values 1-6 behave correctly; only out-of-range handling diverges from the documented contract.

Shipped range 1-6 verified correct.

title: Traceback on closed stdout: mdoutline FILE >&- crashes with AttributeError NoneType
description:
QA re-test t_40226fa7 @ 36d2b75 (Python 3.14.5, Linux, pip-installed console script).

CLAIM (implicit CLI robustness): CLI should degrade with a clean one-line stderr error when stdout is closed, like native tools.

ACTUAL: 'mdoutline FILE >&-' prints a Python traceback to stderr and exits 1:
  File mdoutline.py line 182 in main -> sys.stdout.write(outline)
  AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'write'
(sys.stdout is None when fd 1 is closed; the new BrokenPipeError trap does not catch AttributeError/OSError.)

REPRO: mdoutline any.md >&- ; echo rc=0

NATIVE COMPARISON: cat any.md >&- -> 'cat: standard output: Bad file descriptor', rc 1 (clean one-liner).

FIX DIRECTION: guard sys.stdout is None alongside the existing sys.stdin is None check; catch OSError around the write and emit 'mdoutline: cannot write to standard output: <reason>'.

SEVERITY: Minor/P3 — exotic edge (daemonized/misused fd), cosmetic traceback noise, no data loss. Same write-path robustness class as mdoutline-e52. Route: debugger.

title: ENOSPC on stdout (>/dev/full) prints full traceback instead of clean one-line error
description:
QA re-test t_40226fa7 @ 36d2b75 (Python 3.14.5, Linux, pip-installed console script).

CLAIM (implicit CLI robustness / graceful degradation): on write failure such as disk full, CLI should print one clean stderr line and exit nonzero, like native tools.

ACTUAL: 'mdoutline big.md >/dev/full' prints a multi-line traceback and exits 1:
  File mdoutline.py line 182 in main -> sys.stdout.write(outline)
  OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device
The new BrokenPipeError handler catches only BrokenPipeError; OSError 28 propagates as a traceback. (Note: line-buffered write surfaced here immediately; small outputs can also fail at flush.)

REPRO: python3 -c "open('/tmp/big.md','w').write(''.join('# H'+str(i)+chr(10) for i in range(200000)))"; mdoutline /tmp/big.md >/dev/full

NATIVE COMPARISON: cat /tmp/big.md >/dev/full -> 'cat: standard output: No space left on device', rc 1 (clean one-liner).

FIX DIRECTION: broaden the write-path except clause to OSError (handling BrokenPipeError's SIGPIPE-style exit first), print one-line error, return 1.

SEVERITY: Minor/P3 — edge condition, cosmetic traceback noise + correct rc; real-world disk-full scenario for scripted use. Same write-path class as mdoutline-e52. Route: debugger.

title: BrokenPipeError traceback leaks to stderr when consumer closes pipe early (mdoutline FILE | head)
description:
QA re-test t_1075174f @ 72f6be4 (Python 3.14.5, Linux, pip-installed console script).

CLAIM (implicit CLI robustness / Unix idiom): 'mdoutline FILE | head -n' should degrade silently like standard CLIs.

ACTUAL: When the downstream consumer exits before mdoutline finishes writing, mdoutline raises an unhandled BrokenPipeError: traceback is printed to stderr and exit code is 1.

REPRO (deterministic):
  python3 -c "open('/tmp/big.md','w').write(''.join(f'#{chr(35)*(i%6+1)} Heading {i}'+chr(10) for i in range(200000)))"
  mdoutline /tmp/big.md | head -2
  -> Traceback ... File 'mdoutline.py', line 170, in main
     sys.stdout.write(outline)
     BrokenPipeError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe
  -> PIPESTATUS[0] = 1

OUTPUT CORRECTNESS: the lines head() consumed are delivered correctly; only failure mode is noise + nonzero rc.

FIX SUGGESTION: wrap the write in try/except BrokenPipeError (exit 0 or 141), and/or devnull-dup stdout before interpreter exit to suppress the secondary flush error.

SEVERITY: Minor/P3 — cosmetic traceback in a common pipe idiom; no data loss. Route: debugger.
close_reason: Fixed by 36d2b75. QA re-test t_40226fa7 verified: 0-byte stderr, consumer lines delivered, SIGPIPE-style rc 13 (matches native 'seq' at 141 family — documented). Distinct stdout closed-fd and ENOSPC edges split into mdoutline-0s9/v0f.

title: UTF-8 BOM on first line silently drops the file's first heading
description:
QA re-test t_64d567c7 @ 227c19c (Python 3.14.6, Linux).

CLAIM: spec 'It must work on real-world Markdown'.

OBSERVED (exploratory, beyond spec): extract_headings(['\ufeff# Title', '## A']) -> [(2, 'A')]. The BOM prefixes the '#', so the line does not start with '#' and is not recognized as a heading — the file's h1 silently disappears from the outline. Common for Windows-authored files saved as UTF-8-with-BOM.

REPRO: python3 -c "import mdoutline; print(mdoutline.extract_headings(['\ufeff# Title', '## A']))"

FIX DIRECTION: strip a leading '\ufeff' before the ATX scan (or open files with encoding='utf-8-sig' once the CLI exists).

SEVERITY: Minor/P3 — cosmetic, real-world-frequency edge. Route: debugger.
close_reason: Fixed by 36d2b75 (utf-8-sig on file+stdin). QA re-test t_40226fa7 verified: BOM-prefixed '# Title' now extracted both via FILE arg and stdin, byte-exact od -c evidence; mid-file BOM correctly NOT stripped; no-BOM content byte-identical.

title: Fence closing diverges from CommonMark: info-string closers and shorter closers accepted
description:
QA re-test t_6b5e5c59 @ bfaf57e (Python 3.14.5, Linux).

CLAIM TESTED: spec docs/specs/mdoutline.md 'Fences open/close on lines whose first non-space characters are three or more backticks or tildes (matching char)'. Spec language is loose on closer details; CommonMark 0.31 §Fenced code blocks is the reference standard for 'real-world Markdown'.

ACTUAL (two divergences, both in mdoutline.py:45-64):
1) A closing fence may not carry an info string. 'mdoutline' treats '\`\`\`python' as closing an open backtick fence — CommonMark says it does NOT close (it is a content line). Content after it is parsed as Markdown.
   REPRO: python3 -c "import mdoutline; print(mdoutline.extract_headings(['# Doc','\`\`\`','\`\`\`python','# comment inside example','\`\`\`','# After']))"
   -> [(1,'Doc'), (1,'comment inside example')]   (expected only Doc, After)

2) Closing fence must be at least as long as the opener. Implementation closes a '\`\`\`\`' (4-backtick) fence on '\`\`\`' (3) — CommonMark requires closer >= opener length.
   REPRO: python3 -c "import mdoutline; print(mdoutline.extract_headings(['# Doc','\`\`\`\`','# inner','\`\`\`','# still inner per CommonMark','\`\`\`\`','# After']))"
   -> [(1,'Doc'), (1,'still inner per CommonMark')]   (expected only Doc, After)

Both affect real-world notes: fenced examples that embed a bare-fence line inside a longer fence (very common in Markdown tool documentation). Outcome is over-suppression (headings dropped from the outline) — wrong outline, not a crash.

SEVERITY: Minor/P3 — edge case, no data loss, workaround is editing the note. Overlaps in spirit with prior bead mdoutline-3o7 (CommonMark divergence in heading-close parsing) but is a distinct code path (fence-close validation vs heading text strip).

FIX HINT: when in_fence, require closer to have same char, count >= 3, count >= opener_count, and no non-space trailing content (info-string check).

NOTE: no epic bead exists in this repo's beads DB — no parent to link. Origin card: t_6b5e5c59.

title: Trailing-# stripping ignores CommonMark closing-sequence rule: '## C#' loses its '#'
description:
QA re-test t_543b747a @ 9083542 (Python 3.14.6, Linux).

CLAIM TESTED: spec 'trailing closing #s are stripped from the text' — implementation must only strip #s that form a CommonMark closing sequence (preceded by a space/tab).

ACTUAL: extract_headings strips ANY trailing #s plus preceding whitespace, no space required.
- '## C#'  -> (2, 'C')    expected (2, 'C#')
- '# foo#' -> (1, 'foo')  expected (1, 'foo#')
- '## T##' -> (2, 'T')    expected (2, 'T##')

REPRO: python3 -c "import mdoutline; print(mdoutline.extract_headings(['## C#']))"
-> [(2, 'C')]

IMPACT: headings about C#/F# or ending in # lose characters. mdoutline.py:96-106 strips trailing #s unconditionally (the while loops never check for a whitespace boundary before the hash run). Unit tests only cover the space-separated variants (tests/test_mdoutline.py: test_trailing_closing_hashes_stripped, test_trailing_hashes_with_whitespace_stripped), so this is untested territory, not a regression.

SEVERITY: Minor/P3 — cosmetic edge case, does not block shipping. Spec language is arguably ambiguous; CommonMark semantics say keep the #.

NOTE: no epic bead exists in this repo's beads DB (freshly initialized for this QA cycle) — no parent to link. Origin card: t_543b747a.

title: conftest: resolver-empty env fails suite with generic not-found message; malformed MDOUTLINE_BIN indistinguishable from not-installed
description:
QA re-test t_5fdd7e20 @ 76db60b (2026-08-17).

CLAIM CONTEXT: F3 fix (malformed MDOUTLINE_BIN -> resolver-empty) works correctly at the resolver and guarded-test level. Residual diagnostic gap in the unguarded run_cli path.

OBSERVED: With MDOUTLINE_BIN set but unparseable (e.g. unclosed quote), resolve_mdoutline_cmd returns None (correct), and 132 run_cli-based tests fail with: RuntimeError: mdoutline command not found - set MDOUTLINE_BIN or install the package. The message is misleading in this scenario: MDOUTLINE_BIN IS set (malformed), so the operator is directed to install rather than fix the override syntax.

REPRO: cd /home/lpaydat/workspace/mdoutline && MDOUTLINE_BIN='"unclosed' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q  -> 132 failed, 150 passed, 8 skipped. Failure mode at prior PASS abae99b was worse (96F on the 3 migrated files, FileNotFoundError garbage-argv exec), so this is pre-existing, NOT a regression from 76db60b; strictly improved.

SUGGESTION (test-infra only, no prod impact): when MDOUTLINE_BIN is set but shlex-unparseable, raise/skip with a message naming the actual problem, e.g. 'MDOUTLINE_BIN is set but unparseable (unclosed quote?)'. Loud-fail (not auto-skip) is the right call to avoid skip-as-fix; only the diagnostic text needs to distinguish the two causes. Could live in resolve_mdoutline_cmd returning a reason, or _require_cmd_and_env re-checking the env var.

ENV: CachyOS Linux, Python 3.14.5, pytest 9.1.1, mdoutline 0.1.0 editable, HEAD 76db60be62d7.
notes: UPDATE (re-test t_493d37a2 @ 6d78268): T7 runner-level fallback materially changes this bead's landscape. Live evidence: env MDOUTLINE_BIN='"unclosed-quote' pytest tests/test_cli.py -> 21 passed + 1 skip, RC=0 — the resolver-empty RuntimeError no longer fires (runner falls back to [sys.executable, -m, mdoutline]). The two failure modes are STILL indistinguishable to the operator (no warning on fallback); observability gap now tracked as mdoutline-47y (P3, child of q56). This bead's remaining substance (distinguish malformed vs not-installed) is subsumed by 47y.

title: conftest whitespace-MDOUTLINE_BIN fallthrough fix (abae99b) has no regression test

CLAIM TESTED: commit abae99b ('T2 review iteration 3 - whitespace-only MDOUTLINE_BIN falls through to which() resolution') changes tests/conftest.py:30 resolve_mdoutline_cmd so shlex.split-empty env values (whitespace-only MDOUTLINE_BIN) no longer yield an empty command list.

BUT grep for MDOUTLINE_BIN across tests/ shows zero tests exercising whitespace-only env values: test_behavior_numbers.py:70 and test_behavior_depth.py:72 both use os.environ.get('MDOUTLINE_BIN') for their own _cli() fallback but none set it to whitespace. title: CLI: --help documents --max-depth range as '1-6' but any N≥1 (e.g. 7, 99) is accepted silently
description:
QA re-test @ 81558cd (card t_d536ae2b). Observation, not a regression (prod byte-identical to prior PASS).

CLAIM: help text says '--max-depth N  maximum heading depth to include (1-6, default: all depths)'.
ACTUAL: N=7 or N=99 is accepted, output identical to no filtering (md5-equal on journey doc). N=0 yields empty outline, N<0 → argparse error rc=2.
ANALYSIS: spec (docs/specs/mdoutline.md:37) defines semantics as 'keep headings with depth ≤ N', so accepting 7+ is spec-consistent (all real headings are ≤6). The '1-6' in help reads like a validated range but is advisory. Doc nit only.

REPRO: mdoutline --max-depth 99 FILE | md5sum; mdoutline FILE | md5sum  (identical)
ENV: Python 3.14.5, fresh pip install of mdoutline 0.1.0 @ 81558cd, Linux.

title: conftest run_cli seam API mismatch: fixture takes list-args, legacy call sites use varargs
description: QA re-test t_c1ff9983 @ 5a05dd9. Observation on tests/conftest.py: new shared run_cli fixture signature is run_cli(args, *, stdin, cwd, timeout) — a single list — while all existing probe call sites (tests/test_behavior_numbers.py, test_behavior_depth.py, test_behavior_numbers_verify.py) call run_cli('--numbers', str(f)) varargs-style. Nothing currently consumes the fixture, so no runtime breakage (verified: 263/263 pytest green, lint/format clean, fresh-venv pip install + smoke green). But the migration in later tickets of the refactor series will hit TypeErrors until each call site is rewritten from varargs to list. Also legacy helpers default to sys.executable -m mdoutline fallback; new seam returns None -> tests skip/fail with RuntimeError('mdoutline command not found'). Recommend: when migrating, either keep varargs (*args) in the shared seam or wrap call sites; and give the None case an explicit skip mechanism. Non-bug/test-infra observation for tech-lead.

title: conftest run_cli seam sets PYTHONPATH=REPO_ROOT: probes test repo source, not installed wheel
description: QA re-test t_c1ff9983 @ 5a05dd9 (VERDICT: PASS, test-only delta). Observation on tests/conftest.py run_cli fixture: it prepends REPO_ROOT to the child's PYTHONPATH, so the mdoutline subprocess always imports /home/lpaydat/workspace/mdoutline/mdoutline.py even when the console script comes from an installed wheel. Evidence (neutral cwd /tmp): plain venv python imports /tmp/qa-venv-.../site-packages/mdoutline.py; with PYTHONPATH=REPO_ROOT it imports repo mdoutline.py. Consequence: after the refactor migrates probes onto this seam, a stale/broken installed wheel would go undetected (probes silently test the source tree instead of the artifact a user installs). Legacy per-module helpers (e.g. tests/test_behavior_numbers.py:80-86) used cwd=REPO_ROOT with no PYTHONPATH, i.e. they tested the installed wheel. If testing the installed artifact is desired, the seam should not set PYTHONPATH (or should make it conditional). Non-bug/test-infra observation for tech-lead.

title: Testability: TestDeploymentReadiness fails spuriously unless console script is on PATH
description: QA re-test @ 6a23435 (t_d67dfc69). tests/test_behavior_depth.py::TestDeploymentReadiness::test_console_script_entry_point_exists (+2 siblings in test_behavior_numbers.py) assert shutil.which('mdoutline') against the ambient PATH. title: number_headings: out-of-contract depths (0/negative/7+) yield silent empty numbers or raw IndexError
description:
Claim tested: number_headings docstring says input is (depth,text) tuples from extract_headings() (bounded 1-6); probed what happens on hand-built out-of-contract input (QA re-test t_b5e6e310 @ 03f0a892deca).

Actual behavior (fresh pip install, python 3.14):
- number_headings([(0,'zero'),(1,'one')]) -> [(0,'zero',''),(1,'one','1.')] — depth 0 silently produces EMPTY number string
- number_headings([(-1,'neg'),(6,'six')]) -> [(-1,'neg',''),(6,'six','0.0.0.0.0.1')] — negative depth silently produces empty string
- number_headings([(7,'seven')]) -> IndexError: list index out of range (raw traceback, no message pointing at depth)

Repro: python -c "import mdoutline; mdoutline.number_headings([(7,'x')])"

Severity rationale: documented input domain is extract_headings output which enforces 1-6, and filter_by_depth shares the same no-validation convention (precedent: tiq closed as expected behavior for out-of-range N). But the asymmetry (some invalid depths silent, one a bare IndexError) makes debugging hand-built tuples harder than a single ValueError("depth must be 1-6"). Note-severity consistency gap, not a shipping blocker.

Evidence: /tmp/qa-evidence/t_b5e6e310/probe_number_headings.py + terminal transcript in card t_b5e6e310.

title: test_behavior_depth.py pipe probe mis-commands CLI in python -m fallback: _cli()[0] drops '-m mdoutline'
description:
QA re-test t_0c760d23 @ a93990b (Python 3.14.5, Linux, fresh non-editable pip install).

FINDING (test-suite quality, not product): TestDeploymentReadiness::test_broken_pipe_is_quiet_nonzero builds its shell command from _cli()[0] alone (tests/test_behavior_depth.py:415 area): cmd = f"'{_cli()[0]}' --max-depth 1 '{big}' | head -n 1 >/dev/null". When the mdoutline console script is NOT on PATH, _cli() falls back to [sys.executable, '-m', 'mdoutline'] (tests/test_behavior_depth.py:75-76); _cli()[0] is then the bare python binary and the probe runs 'python --max-depth 1 FILE', which fails with 'Unknown option: --max-depth' rc=2 instead of exercising the pipe behavior.

REPRO (fresh venv, pip install ., console script not on PATH):
  PATH-without-venv python -m pytest test_behavior_depth.py::TestDeploymentReadiness::test_broken_pipe_is_quiet_nonzero
  -> AssertionError: (2, b"Unknown option: --max-depth ... usage: <python> [option] ...")

IMPACT: misleading failure that looks like a product regression when running the suite outside an activated venv (e.g. make test with system pytest). With the venv on PATH (documented workflow) the test passes. Fix: use ' '.join(map(shlex.quote, _cli())) or subprocess list form. Severity Note/P4. Route: debugger.

title: splitlines() splits on U+2028/U+0085/formfeed: phantom headings from mid-prose text
description:
mdoutline splits input via str.splitlines(), which treats Unicode line separators (U+2028, U+0085), form feed (\\x0c), and file/group separators (\\x1c-\\x1e) as line breaks. A '#' run after any of these characters mid-line is extracted as a heading even though no newline precedes it.

Repro (real bytes):
  printf 'Intro: cost\xe2\x80\xa8## Fake heading\n' > /tmp/u.md && mdoutline /tmp/u.md
Actual: '- Fake heading' (indented, from mid-prose)
Expected: '' (no heading; U+2028 is not a line terminator for line-oriented Markdown scanning)

Found during integration verification of ticket-01 (t_b0a5aac7). Fix: split on '\\n' only (e.g. content.split(chr(10))), or pre-replace exotic separators with newlines. Byte-identical output for pure LF/CRLF/CR input either way.

Triage guidance: same class as other spec-vs-CommonMark divergences (3o7/zpw/c8r) — line-parser edge outside the ticket-01 AC text.

title: CLI: '-' not accepted as stdin alias (Unix convention gap)
description:
QA re-test t_64d567c7 @ 72f6be4 (Python 3.13, Linux, fresh venv editable install).

CLAIM (convention, not spec): Unix CLI convention — '-' as positional file argument means stdin (cat, grep, sort, etc.). Spec froze CLI as 'optional positional file argument' without mentioning '-', so this is a Note-severity convention gap, not a spec violation.

ACTUAL: mdoutline - attempts to open a literal file named '-':
  printf '# Hi\n' | mdoutline -
  -> mdoutline: cannot read '-': No such file or directory  (stderr, exit 1)

REPRO: printf '# Hi\n' | mdoutline - ; echo $?

Suggested batch: fold into the polish ticket with f5w/3o7/ijd/zpw (tab-separator, BOM, closing-seq, fence-closer rules).

title: Spec tighter than CommonMark: tab after # not accepted as heading separator
description:
QA re-test t_543b747a @ bfaf57e (Python 3.14.6, Linux).

OBSERVATION (spec feedback, not an implementation defect):
Stamped spec docs/specs/mdoutline.md says a heading is 1-6 # then 'a space or end of line'. Implementation follows this exactly: '#<TAB>Title' is rejected (not a heading).
CommonMark 0.31 (§ATX headings) accepts one space OR tab after the hashes. Real-world notes pasted from editors that expand to tabs would silently drop such headings.

REPRO: python3 -c "import mdoutline; print(mdoutline.extract_headings(['#\tTab sep', '## A']))"
-> [(2, 'A')]

Route: product-owner (spec decision — widen the spec or accept as-is). Implementation is spec-conformant; no code change warranted unless spec changes.
